problem_statement: This creative-coding shaders demo renders animation studies through Three.js WebGL material shaders animated with the GSAP timeline inside a Vite build. biazo/codrops-animate-shaders-with-gsap is a Codrops Vite + Three.js/WebGL demo animated with GSAP: a fixed minimal masthead frame, a 01/02/03/04 study navigation, a deck of local WebP image plates with captions, a fixed floating bar, four shader study routes (index.html + index2/3/4.html), and a full-viewport pointer-events-none WebGL canvas. The site has been rebranded into the Halcyon Field Lab motion-studies journal. It ships a native on-canvas Study Console - a compact black/white HUD overlaying the top-left of the canvas on every study route - that reads the current study, render mode, frames held and palette in a row of metric tiles, shows a live 'Rendering: <study> . <mode>' readout, and offers a Light / Deep / Draft render-mode selector. The current Study Console is broken: it renders only on study route 01, its metric-tile row is a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows the 390px phone viewport, its tiles have overgrown into oversized near-black slabs that overlap and bury the canvas with illegible dark-on-dark text, and its render-mode buttons toggle their active state without ever re-rendering the readout. Repair the Study Console so it appears on all four study routes, its metric-tile row wraps and stays inside the phone viewport with no horizontal overflow, its tiles are the quiet legible black/white panel of the minimal Codrops system, and clicking a render-mode preset live-updates the 'Rendering: ...' readout - all while preserving the WebGL canvas scene, the GSAP animation logic, the four shader routes, the masthead frame and the local WebP plates exactly as they are.
required_content: Render the Study Console HUD on every study route (index.html + index2/3/4.html), each with a route-specific study-console--01/02/03/04 marker and a live 'Rendering: <study> . <mode>' readout.
Make the metric-tile row (Study route / Render mode / Frames held / Palette) wrap and stay inside the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow of the console panel.
Restyle the console tiles into the quiet legible black-on-white panel of the minimal Codrops system - no overgrown, overlapping, or illegible dark-on-dark tiles that bury the canvas.
Wire the Light / Deep / Draft render-mode selector so clicking a preset live-updates the '#console-readout' text (for example to 'Rendering: Study 01 . DEEP'), not just the button's active state.

Keep the Halcyon Field Lab persona chrome (masthead title, #MOTION-LAB/#LIVE-RENDER/#FIELD-STUDY tags, Field Notes/Study Index/Contact Lab floating bar, persona plate captions) intact across all four routes.
Do not edit src/js/demo* shader code, the Three.js/GSAP material or animation logic, the vite build config, generated dist output, node_modules, or the local WebP image assets.
The Study Console must remain readable on desktop, tablet and 390px mobile and must not cover or break the WebGL canvas, the image deck, or the floating bar.
design_constraints: Treat this as a section-level design-continuity repair of the native Study Console HUD, not a new landing page, a new route, or a shader rewrite.
Follow the existing Codrops design language: white background, black text, gray secondary text, thin rules, uppercase display type, compact spacing, and the fixed masthead + floating-bar layout.
Keep the four shader study routes reachable through the 01/02/03/04 study navigation exactly as before.
Reuse the existing local WebP image plates; do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, remote analytics/ad scripts, or new media.
The Study Console must be present and consistent on every study route - a console on route 01 only is not acceptable.
Preserve the WebGL canvas overlay and GSAP-driven animation behaviour; the visual scene must be unchanged.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures study route 01 with the Study Console overlaying the top-left of the WebGL canvas: the 'RENDER CONSOLE' panel, the 'Rendering: Study 01 . LIGHT' readout, the four metric tiles, and the Light/Deep/Draft selector, alongside the masthead frame, the captioned WebP plates and the floating bar.
mobile_initial captures route 01 at 390px, where the Study Console tile row must wrap and stay inside the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_initial captures route 01 at tablet width.
desktop_console_deep re-captures route 01 after clicking the Deep render-mode preset; the readout must update to 'Rendering: Study 01 . DEEP'.
desktop_variation_02/03/04 capture the other three shader study routes, each with its own Study Console (study-console--02/03/04) over the WebGL canvas and captioned plates.
desktop_tags_regression re-captures route 01 to confirm the masthead tags, study navigation and Study Console still render after the repair.

Source inspection confirms the foreground chrome + Study Console live in index.html + index2/3/4.html and src/css/console.css + src/js/console.js, while the shader scene lives in src/js/demo1..4 (Three.js material + GSAP animation), so the console can be repaired without touching the WebGL logic.

change_completion: The Study Console renders on all four study routes with its route-specific marker and a live 'Rendering: <study> . <mode>' readout.
The render-mode selector (Light/Deep/Draft) live-updates the readout on click rather than only toggling the active button.
design_consistency: The Study Console tiles are the quiet legible black-on-white panel of the minimal Codrops system, not overgrown/overlapping/illegible slabs.
The Halcyon Field Lab persona chrome and the WebGL canvas scene are preserved unchanged across all routes.
regression: The static build still serves the four study routes over a plain static server.
The 01/02/03/04 study navigation and the WebGL canvas continue to render on every route.
responsive: The Study Console metric-tile row wraps and stays inside the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow.
The console, masthead and floating bar coexist without covering the canvas or the plate deck.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Vite/Three.js/WebGL + GSAP interactive_canvas task, hardened to L4 with a native on-canvas Study Console HUD (Halcyon Field Lab motion-studies journal). Four orthogonal levers ride the console: cross-route presence (dom_assertions), a wrapping metric-tile row (no_horizontal_overflow), a legible black/white panel (visual_regression over the console image crops), and a render-mode selector that re-renders the readout (interaction_assertions). Runability passes through the Vite static build served as a plain static site (real 404). The WebGL canvas is a fullscreen pointer-events-none overlay contributing 0 to document width, so the console strip carries the overflow lever cleanly. Headless swiftshader WebGL performance messages are warnings, not errors, and are allow-listed; 0 console errors across all states.
